rationale: CBG is a non-inhibitory serpin. All three annotation lines are family-level inference or an old review. PMID:19643161 and PMID:19011238 describe CBG explicitly as non-inhibitory and show the RCL is cleaved by elastase without inhibition. Classic serpin-family over-annotation.

recommended_action: RETAIN and add a more specific child
rationale: Correct but non-specific. GO:1903794 cortisol binding is supported by Scatchard Kd 0.64 nM (PMID:1504007) and by 13 first-shell contacts in 2VDY/4C49. GO:1990239 steroid hormone binding is an intermediate option. Progesterone binding is also structurally documented (4BB2).
Most informative MF term the evidence supports. PMID:1504007 gives wild-type Kd 0.64 +/- 0.31 nM; PMID:18513745 and PDB 2VDY/4C49 give the cortisol-bound structure.
Captures the transport function that distinguishes CBG from inhibitory serpins. Pairs with the proteinase-triggered release mechanism in PMID:17644521 and PMID:18513745.

CBG binds and delivers cortisol; it does not catalyse any step of glucocorticoid synthesis. A transport or bioavailability term (for example GO:0009914 hormone transport) describes the gene product activity better. Pathway-membership carry-over from Reactome.
